disease.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease

overview.description: Peptic Ulcer Disease involves open sores (ulcers) that develop on the inner lining of the stomach (gastric ulcers) or the upper part of the small intestine (duodenal ulcers). It results from an imbalance between aggressive factors (acid, pepsin) and protective mucosal defenses. Most cases are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection or long-term NSAID use.
overview.prevalence: Affects millions worldwide; approximately 4-5 million new cases annually.
overview.age_group: Adults; duodenal ulcers peak in 30-50 years, gastric ulcers more common after 60 years

anatomy_and_physiology.disease_mechanism: Imbalance between aggressive factors (acid, pepsin) and protective mucosal defenses.

types.name: Gastric Ulcer
types.description: Ulcers located in the stomach lining. Pain often worsens with food intake.
types.common_in: Older adults, NSAID users, H. pylori infection

types.name: Duodenal Ulcer
types.description: Ulcers in the first part of the small intestine (duodenum). Pain often improves with food or antacids.
types.common_in: Younger to middle-aged adults, H. pylori positive cases

types.name: Marginal / Stomal Ulcer
types.description: Ulcers occurring at the site of surgical anastomosis (after stomach surgery).

severity_levels.name: Mild / Uncomplicated
severity_levels.frequency: Intermittent epigastric pain, responsive to treatment
severity_levels.impact: Managed outpatient with medications and lifestyle changes

severity_levels.name: Moderate with Bleeding
severity_levels.impact: Requires hospitalization, endoscopy, and acid suppression

severity_levels.name: Severe / Complicated
severity_levels.impact: Surgical emergency with high risk of complications

genetic_factors: Blood group O (increased risk for duodenal ulcers)
Genetic predisposition to higher acid secretion
environmental_triggers: High psychological stress (in critically ill patients)

primary_symptoms.name: Burning Epigastric Pain
primary_symptoms.description: Gnawing or burning pain in the upper abdomen, often between meals or at night.

secondary_symptoms: Loss of appetite and weight loss (especially gastric ulcers)
Intolerance to fatty or spicy foods
warning_signs_of_attack: Dizziness, fainting, or rapid heartbeat due to blood loss
symptoms_in_children: Poor weight gain or growth failure

medical_history: Symptom pattern and relation to meals
physical_examination: Signs of anemia or peritonitis (in complications)

diagnostic_tests.description: Urea breath test, stool antigen, or rapid urease test during endoscopy.
Direct visualization and biopsy of ulcers.
diagnostic_tests.purpose: Gold standard for diagnosis and ruling out cancer

medicines.note: All medications should be taken only under the supervision of a licensed physician. Self-medication can be dangerous.

categories.purpose: Strongly suppress stomach acid production to promote ulcer healing

medicines.name: Omeprazole
medicines.use_case: First-line acid suppression for ulcer healing

categories.purpose: Reduce acid secretion (less potent than PPIs)
Combination antibiotics + PPI to eliminate H. pylori
categories.note: Typically 10-14 days course; bismuth quadruple therapy preferred in many regions

medicines.name: Clarithromycin + Amoxicillin + PPI
medicines.dosage: Standard doses twice daily for 14 days

medicines.name: Bismuth + Metronidazole + Tetracycline + PPI
medicines.use_case: Preferred in high clarithromycin resistance areas

categories.purpose: Neutralize acid or coat the ulcer

trigger_avoidance: Avoid NSAIDs; use alternatives if needed
Practice good hygiene to prevent H. pylori spread

recommended: Light to moderate exercise like walking
precautions: Avoid strenuous activity during acute pain

green_zone.symptoms: Minimal or no pain; following treatment

yellow_zone.action: Take antacids/PPI as prescribed; consult doctor

red_zone.symptoms: Vomiting blood, black stools, severe pain

diet_and_nutrition.overview: While no specific diet cures ulcers, avoiding irritants and eating balanced meals supports healing and symptom relief.

items.benefit: Gentle on stomach, helps absorb acid
Supports gut health, may help fight H. pylori

foods_to_avoid.reason: Stimulate acid production and damage mucosa

sample_meal_plan.note: Eat small, frequent meals. Avoid eating close to bedtime.
sample_meal_plan.breakfast: Oatmeal with banana and a little honey
sample_meal_plan.lunch: Grilled chicken, steamed rice, cooked vegetables
sample_meal_plan.dinner: Baked fish, mashed potatoes, boiled spinach
sample_meal_plan.before_bed: Warm milk (if tolerated) or chamomile tea

special_dietary_notes: Avoid lying down immediately after meals

trigger_avoidance: Avoid NSAIDs; use alternatives if needed
Practice good hygiene to prevent H. pylori spread

recommended: Light to moderate exercise like walking
precautions: Avoid strenuous activity during acute pain

complications.description: Ulcer erodes a blood vessel causing hemorrhage.
Ulcer breaks through the stomach/duodenal wall.
Especially with chronic H. pylori infection.

key_points: Higher risk due to NSAID use and comorbidities
PPIs generally safe; H. pylori testing if needed

emergency_signs: Signs of shock (rapid pulse, cold clammy skin)

faq.question: Can peptic ulcers be cured?
faq.answer: Yes. Most ulcers heal completely with proper treatment, especially after H. pylori eradication.

faq.question: Do spicy foods cause ulcers?
faq.answer: No. They do not cause ulcers but can worsen symptoms in some people.

faq.question: How long does it take for an ulcer to heal?
faq.answer: With treatment, most ulcers heal in 4-8 weeks.
